reference: Native @google/adk 2.3.0 browser bundle (dist/web/index_web.js) driven by its own Runner, run on Node
normalizations: Function-call and function-response IDs are runtime-generated on each side (ADK uses adk-<uuid>, galaxie uses galaxie-<n>), so transcripts compare names and payloads only.

Requests are recorded at the ADK model boundary on both sides: the scripted BaseLlm on the native side and a wrapper around host.adk.llm(role) on the galaxie side. The galaxie scripted replies come from the deterministic mock chat model behind the router.

Run errors compare by code. ADK reports a failed run as an error event whose code is UNKNOWN_ERROR or INVOCATION_ABORTED; the native harness maps its call-limit message to budget_exceeded, an aborted invocation to cancelled, and its own host-check emulation to denied.

The native lane emulates the host output-safety hook with the same BLOCKED_ pattern the galaxie run uses; the native lane has no router, so this stands in for the host hook only to keep the case comparable.
A request that galaxie's step budget refuses before dispatch is dropped from the galaxie transcript, because ADK's call limit refuses before it asks the model.

Streaming cases run the native Runner in SSE mode with a scripted model that yields one partial response per word before the final response; the galaxie lane runs SSE through the router with the mock chat model's word chunks. Both sides record the partial text deltas in order and the content-free tool step markers (step kind, offered tool name, position). The other cases compare complete responses only: the galaxie wrapper drops partial responses, which exist only because the adapter always runs ADK in SSE mode.

Approval cases register the same tool with confirmation required on both sides. The native lane runs a second invocation whose user message carries the confirmation function response; the galaxie lane answers the interaction with the default resume (action approve or deny, payload { indexes: [0] }). Both record the tool calls the run paused on (name and arguments, never a call ID), the model requests including the tool result or the denial text the model sees, the capability calls and the final output.
limits: Duplicate identity outcome (2026-11-13), superseding the earlier ambiguity limit: D-js REFUSED; any repeated agent name including root reuse fails unsupported at prepare before model or store access. Exact case/NFC/NFD distinctions and unique-name restore bytes are preserved. Message-only attribution is unambiguous for accepted trees; subgraphs stays false. Node/Chromium scripted evidence in duplicate-identity-native.test.ts and duplicate-identity-measure.test.ts.

Model/toolset/builtin spike: M-js and T-js ALTERNATIVE through fresh helper-built models and flat capability lists; N-js/X-js/L-js REFUSED. String mapping fails repeated-prepare idempotence. Provider tool config is rejected, not silently dropped. New scripted Node/Chromium characterizations; no runtime, golden or existing case changes.

Stream namespace spike: A-js/C-js ALTERNATIVE (message-only author/tree lookup; GA3 duplicate-name ambiguity); B-js REFUSED (manifest-only routing and full routed replacement not established). Node/Chromium scripted probes; no source, flag, path or record changes.

Stage A5 adds durable sessions: with a byte-record checkpoint port in the host services, a pause and each completed conversation are stored as an adk.session/v1 record, and a reload restores the pause through core's restore. Failed and cancelled runs write nothing, partial events and binary parts are never stored, and a stored record is validated against a closed schema before ADK sees it. The adapter reports streaming, interrupts, resume and checkpoints as true and subgraphs as false. The restore lanes are in adk-restore.test.ts, not the golden cases, because they need a second runtime lifetime.
The run input is { prompt: string }. Only the closed set of LlmAgent, SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent and LoopAgent is accepted, and tools and models must come from the host.
All model replies are deterministic scripts; no real model, network request or download takes part.
The Chromium lane runs under the vitest browser project, not a page with the strict mock CSP; the strict-CSP bundle probe in packages/adapter-adk covers the bundle alone.

Agent shapes: SequentialAgent, LoopAgent, ParallelAgent and an LlmAgent with sub-agents and transfer match native ADK in model requests and output (packages/adapter-adk/test/agents.test.ts), and parallel write branches replay their own receipts after a re-dispatch with reversed arrival. ADK resumes directly at the paused agent only when it and all its ancestors are LlmAgents, and otherwise restarts from the root (native SequentialAgent evidence in agents.test.ts), so a pause inside a loop, a later sequential child, under an LlmAgent inside a workflow agent, in a tree containing a ParallelAgent, or by an unknown or duplicate-named agent fails unsupported; a pause in the first child at every sequential step, or in an LlmAgent chain linked by transfer, resumes in place and survives a reload. subgraphs stays false: ADK events carry author and branch, not LangGraph namespaces, and nested stream paths and nested-pause parity are not built. AgentTool and Workflow fail unsupported at prepare.

ADK drops the function responses of sibling calls that ran beside a confirmation-gated call in the same model turn, so the adapter fails such a turn as unsupported, as it does a confirmation beside a long-running call, a pause inside a ParallelAgent and a long-running call whose result never arrives. ADK also hides adk_request_input calls and answers from an LlmAgent, so a pause on that tool fails as unsupported.
